node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"

The coverage flow:
1. `nyc instrument` the tree
2. Run the node harness (`node_testRunner.js`) against the instrumented copy
3. `crap4js` with the baseline

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"

1. `nyc instrument` the tree
2. Run the node harness (`node_testRunner.js`) against the instrumented copy

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"

1. `nyc instrument` the tree
2. Run the node harness (`node_testRunner.js`) against the instrumented copy
3. `crap4js` with the baseline

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"

The coverage flow:
1. `nyc instrument` the tree
2. Run the node harness (`node_testRunner.js`) against the instrumented copy
3. `crap4js` with the baseline

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"

### `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` (CC 51, CRAP 1512.8)

The action has these phases:

2. Config/SCM/tracker creation

5. PR resolution: findTestPRForTicket or (no PR): branch-exists check → back-out to Backlog OR checkout (with fetch fallback) + auto-create PR (success → continue; fail → noPR return)
6. PR details fetch

8. Merge conflict detection + diff + discussions

Extraction plan for preCliTestReworkSetup (pure planners, side effects stay in order):
- `resolveTicketContext(params)` — pure: resolves inputFolder/ticketKey. Small CC.
- `buildReworkStartedComment(prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure: builds the Jira comment string (with conflicts panel). This has the conflicts loop.
- `decideNoPrOutcome(...)` — hmm, the no-PR flow has: ls-remote probe (side effect), tracker calls (side effect), checkout (side effect), createPr (side effect). 

Better approach following "Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor":
- `buildReworkStartedComment(ticketKey, prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure, testable.
- `buildBranchMissingError(testBranchName)` — trivial.

CRAP = CC² + CC (at 0% coverage) — actually CRAP = CC² * (1 - cov)³ + CC - 1... the standard formula: CRAP = comp² * (1 - coverage)³ + comp. At 100% coverage CRAP = comp - 1. Hmm, for crap4js let me check the formula. Actually standard crap4j: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. At 0% coverage: CRAP = comp² + comp. At 100%: CRAP = comp − 1... 

For action with CC 51 at 17.5% coverage: 51² × (1-0.175)³ + 51 = 2601 × 0.5615 + 51 ≈ 1460 + 51 = 1511. ✓ matches 1512.8 (coverage slightly different).

To get action < 100:

After extraction, the remaining action body will be: resolve params, load config/scm/tracker, clear stale outputs, repoInfo check, ensurePr (call helper), PR details check, checkout, conflicts, diff, discussions, context write, questions, bugs, comment, return. If I extract the no-PR flow into `ensureTestPullRequest(scm, tracker, config, ticketKey, inputFolder, cli)` and the comment building into a pure function, action's CC should drop to ~12-15. With coverage ~90%+, CRAP ≈ 15² × (0.1)³ + 14 = 0.15 + 14 ≈ 14.

Wait — re-read: "new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it)". So a new function with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 12 - 1 = 11 > 8 → blocked as newOverThreshold! Hmm, but that would mean EVERY extracted helper must have CRAP ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage. At 100% coverage, CRAP = CC - 1 ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9. OK so extracted helpers can have up to CC 9 if fully covered. That's fine.

But wait — is coverage in the node harness (with ~108 known mock-gap failures) going to give the helpers 100% coverage? The coverage comes from the node harness run over ALL test files in run_all.json. My new tests will run there. Coverage of partially-covered helpers: a helper with CC 12 at 85% coverage → 144 × (0.15)³ + 11 = 0.486 + 11 = 11.5 → still > 8 → FAIL. So helpers need CC ≤ 8ish or very high coverage.

Rule of thumb for me: keep extracted helpers CC ≤ 9 and make sure tests cover all branches. For bigger extracted pieces (like the no-PR flow, CC ~20), split into multiple smaller helpers, OR ensure coverage is ~95%+: CC 20 at 95% → 400 × (0.05)³ + 19 = 0.05 + 19 ≈ 19 → still > 8. CRAP at high coverage ≈ CC - 1. So EVERY new function must have CC ≤ 9 regardless (given near-100% coverage). OK: max CC 9 per new function, fully covered.

Hmm wait, but also existing over-threshold functions I extract FROM: the ratchet only compares functions that exist in BOTH baseline and metrics.           # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"

### `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` (CC 51, CRAP 1512.8)

The action has these phases:
1. Param/inputFolder/ticketKey resolution
2. Config/SCM/tracker creation
3. Stale output clearing (cli call)
4. repoInfo check
5. PR resolution: findTestPRForTicket or (no PR): branch-exists check → back-out to Backlog OR checkout (with fetch fallback) + auto-create PR (success → continue; fail → noPR return)
6. PR details fetch
7. Branch determination + checkout
8. Merge conflict detection + diff + discussions
9. Context write
10. Questions/bugs fetch
11. Jira comment build (with conflicts panel)
12. Success return

Extraction plan for preCliTestReworkSetup (pure planners, side effects stay in order):
- `resolveTicketContext(params)` — pure: resolves inputFolder/ticketKey. Small CC.
- `buildReworkStartedComment(prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure: builds the Jira comment string (with conflicts panel). This has the conflicts loop.
- `decideNoPrOutcome(...)` — hmm, the no-PR flow has: ls-remote probe (side effect), tracker calls (side effect), checkout (side effect), createPr (side effect). 

Better approach following "Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor":
- `buildReworkStartedComment(ticketKey, prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure, testable.
- `buildBranchMissingError(testBranchName)` — trivial.
- The no-PR flow can be extracted into `ensureTestBranchAndPr(...)` — a helper function with its own CC, but then the helper needs to be covered by tests (which my characterization tests do — the auto-create paths are covered now).

CRAP = CC² + CC (at 0% coverage) — actually CRAP = CC² * (1 - cov)³ + CC - 1... the standard formula: CRAP = comp² * (1 - coverage)³ + comp. At 100% coverage CRAP = comp - 1. Hmm, for crap4js let me check the formula. Actually standard crap4j: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. At 0% coverage: CRAP = comp² + comp. At 100%: CRAP = comp − 1... 

For action with CC 51 at 17.5% coverage: 51² × (1-0.175)³ + 51 = 2601 × 0.5615 + 51 ≈ 1460 + 51 = 1511. ✓ matches 1512.8 (coverage slightly different).

To get action < 100:
- Option A: CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 8. Or CC 11 at ~90% coverage: 121 × 0.001 + 11 ≈ 11. 
- So I need to cut action's CC from 51 to ~≤10 AND have it well covered.

My characterization tests cover most paths of action. After extraction, the remaining action body will be: resolve params, load config/scm/tracker, clear stale outputs, repoInfo check, ensurePr (call helper), PR details check, checkout, conflicts, diff, discussions, context write, questions, bugs, comment, return. If I extract the no-PR flow into `ensureTestPullRequest(scm, tracker, config, ticketKey, inputFolder, cli)` and the comment building into a pure function, action's CC should drop to ~12-15. With coverage ~90%+, CRAP ≈ 15² × (0.1)³ + 14 = 0.15 + 14 ≈ 14. 

New functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP if untested → CC ≤ 2, or cover them. My tests will cover the extracted helpers well (through action and directly for pure ones). A helper with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP 11 — that's > 8, which FAILS the ratchet for NEW functions ("new functions must be <= 8")! 

Wait — re-read: "new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it)". So a new function with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 12 - 1 = 11 > 8 → blocked as newOverThreshold! Hmm, but that would mean EVERY extracted helper must have CRAP ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage. At 100% coverage, CRAP = CC - 1 ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9. OK so extracted helpers can have up to CC 9 if fully covered. That's fine.

But wait — is coverage in the node harness (with ~108 known mock-gap failures) going to give the helpers 100% coverage? The coverage comes from the node harness run over ALL test files in run_all.json. My new tests will run there. Coverage of partially-covered helpers: a helper with CC 12 at 85% coverage → 144 × (0.15)³ + 11 = 0.486 + 11 = 11.5 → still > 8 → FAIL. So helpers need CC ≤ 8ish or very high coverage.

Rule of thumb for me: keep extracted helpers CC ≤ 9 and make sure tests cover all branches. For bigger extracted pieces (like the no-PR flow, CC ~20), split into multiple smaller helpers, OR ensure coverage is ~95%+: CC 20 at 95% → 400 × (0.05)³ + 19 = 0.05 + 19 ≈ 19 → still > 8. CRAP at high coverage ≈ CC - 1. So EVERY new function must have CC ≤ 9 regardless (given near-100% coverage). OK: max CC 9 per new function, fully covered.

Hmm wait, but also existing over-threshold functions I extract FROM: the ratchet only compares functions that exist in BOTH baseline and metrics. If I delete `action` (rename), the baseline key `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` would be "removed" — and `removed` doesn't fail. But the ticket wants `action` to remain (same exports/signatures). `action` will remain in the baseline with its key. Its score must go DOWN from 1512.8. If I re-extract so its CC drops to ~10 with ~95% coverage → CRAP ≈ 10 → improved. 

Also "no function may go up": `findTestPRForTicket` (30 in preCli file, 42 in post file) must not go up. I won't touch them, or may even improve them.

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"

The coverage flow:
1. `nyc instrument` the tree
2. Run the node harness (`node_testRunner.js`) against the instrumented copy
3. `crap4js` with the baseline

blocks.text:
While instrumentation runs, let me plan the refactoring. Let me analyze the complexity hotspots.

### `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` (CC 51, CRAP 1512.8)

The action has these phases:
1. Param/inputFolder/ticketKey resolution
2. Config/SCM/tracker creation
3. Stale output clearing (cli call)
4. repoInfo check
5. PR resolution: findTestPRForTicket or (no PR): branch-exists check → back-out to Backlog OR checkout (with fetch fallback) + auto-create PR (success → continue; fail → noPR return)
6. PR details fetch
7. Branch determination + checkout
8. Merge conflict detection + diff + discussions
9. Context write
10. Questions/bugs fetch
11. Jira comment build (with conflicts panel)
12. Success return

Extraction plan for preCliTestReworkSetup (pure planners, side effects stay in order):
- `resolveTicketContext(params)` — pure: resolves inputFolder/ticketKey. Small CC.
- `buildReworkStartedComment(prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure: builds the Jira comment string (with conflicts panel). This has the conflicts loop.
- `decideNoPrOutcome(...)` — hmm, the no-PR flow has: ls-remote probe (side effect), tracker calls (side effect), checkout (side effect), createPr (side effect). 

Better approach following "Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor":
- `buildReworkStartedComment(ticketKey, prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure, testable.
- `buildBranchMissingError(testBranchName)` — trivial.
- The no-PR flow can be extracted into `ensureTestBranchAndPr(...)` — a helper function with its own CC, but then the helper needs to be covered by tests (which my characterization tests do — the auto-create paths are covered now).

CRAP = CC² + CC (at 0% coverage) — actually CRAP = CC² * (1 - cov)³ + CC - 1... the standard formula: CRAP = comp² * (1 - coverage)³ + comp. At 100% coverage CRAP = comp - 1. Hmm, for crap4js let me check the formula. Actually standard crap4j: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. At 0% coverage: CRAP = comp² + comp. At 100%: CRAP = comp − 1... 

For action with CC 51 at 17.5% coverage: 51² × (1-0.175)³ + 51 = 2601 × 0.5615 + 51 ≈ 1460 + 51 = 1511. ✓ matches 1512.8 (coverage slightly different).

To get action < 100:
- Option A: CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 8. Or CC 11 at ~90% coverage: 121 × 0.001 + 11 ≈ 11.

My characterization tests cover most paths of action. node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"

1. `nyc instrument` the tree
2. Run the node harness (`node_testRunner.js`) against the instrumented copy

### `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` (CC 51, CRAP 1512.8)

The action has these phases:

2. Config/SCM/tracker creation
3. Stale output clearing (cli call)
4. repoInfo check
5. PR resolution: findTestPRForTicket or (no PR): branch-exists check → back-out to Backlog OR checkout (with fetch fallback) + auto-create PR (success → continue; fail → noPR return)
6. PR details fetch
7. Branch determination + checkout
8. Merge conflict detection + diff + discussions
9. Context write
10. Questions/bugs fetch
11. Jira comment build (with conflicts panel)
12. Success return

Extraction plan for preCliTestReworkSetup (pure planners, side effects stay in order):
- `resolveTicketContext(params)` — pure: resolves inputFolder/ticketKey. Small CC.
- `buildReworkStartedComment(prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure: builds the Jira comment string (with conflicts panel). This has the conflicts loop.
- `decideNoPrOutcome(...)` — hmm, the no-PR flow has: ls-remote probe (side effect), tracker calls (side effect), checkout (side effect), createPr (side effect). 

Better approach following "Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor":
- `buildReworkStartedComment(ticketKey, prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure, testable.
- `buildBranchMissingError(testBranchName)` — trivial.
- The no-PR flow can be extracted into `ensureTestBranchAndPr(...)` — a helper function with its own CC, but then the helper needs to be covered by tests (which my characterization tests do — the auto-create paths are covered now).

CRAP = CC² + CC (at 0% coverage) — actually CRAP = CC² * (1 - cov)³ + CC - 1... the standard formula: CRAP = comp² * (1 - coverage)³ + comp. At 100% coverage CRAP = comp - 1. Hmm, for crap4js let me check the formula. Actually standard crap4j: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. At 0% coverage: CRAP = comp² + comp. At 100%: CRAP = comp − 1... 

For action with CC 51 at 17.5% coverage: 51² × (1-0.175)³ + 51 = 2601 × 0.5615 + 51 ≈ 1460 + 51 = 1511. ✓ matches 1512.8 (coverage slightly different).

To get action < 100:
- Option A: CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 8. Or CC 11 at ~90% coverage: 121 × 0.001 + 11 ≈ 11. 
- So I need to cut action's CC from 51 to ~≤10 AND have it well covered.

My characterization tests cover most paths of action. After extraction, the remaining action body will be: resolve params, load config/scm/tracker, clear stale outputs, repoInfo check, ensurePr (call helper), PR details check, checkout, conflicts, diff, discussions, context write, questions, bugs, comment, return. If I extract the no-PR flow into `ensureTestPullRequest(scm, tracker, config, ticketKey, inputFolder, cli)` and the comment building into a pure function, action's CC should drop to ~12-15. With coverage ~90%+, CRAP ≈ 15² × (0.1)³ + 14 = 0.15 + 14 ≈ 14. 

New functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP if untested → CC ≤ 2, or cover them. My tests will cover the extracted helpers well (through action and directly for pure ones). A helper with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP 11 — that's > 8, which FAILS the ratchet for NEW functions ("new functions must be <= 8")! 

Wait — re-read: "new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it)". So a new function with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 12 - 1 = 11 > 8 → blocked as newOverThreshold! Hmm, but that would mean EVERY extracted helper must have CRAP ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage. At 100% coverage, CRAP = CC - 1 ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9. OK so extracted helpers can have up to CC 9 if fully covered. That's fine.

But wait — is coverage in the node harness (with ~108 known mock-gap failures) going to give the helpers 100% coverage? The coverage comes from the node harness run over ALL test files in run_all.json. My new tests will run there. Coverage of partially-covered helpers: a helper with CC 12 at 85% coverage → 144 × (0.15)³ + 11 = 0.486 + 11 = 11.5 → still > 8 → FAIL. So helpers need CC ≤ 8ish or very high coverage.

Rule of thumb for me: keep extracted helpers CC ≤ 9 and make sure tests cover all branches. For bigger extracted pieces (like the no-PR flow, CC ~20), split into multiple smaller helpers, OR ensure coverage is ~95%+: CC 20 at 95% → 400 × (0.05)³ + 19 = 0.05 + 19 ≈ 19 → still > 8. CRAP at high coverage ≈ CC - 1. So EVERY new function must have CC ≤ 9 regardless (given near-100% coverage). OK: max CC 9 per new function, fully covered.

Hmm wait, but also existing over-threshold functions I extract FROM: the ratchet only compares functions that exist in BOTH baseline and metrics. node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"

The coverage flow:
1. `nyc instrument` the tree
2. Run the node harness (`node_testRunner.js`) against the instrumented copy
3. `crap4js` with the baseline

6. PR details fetch

12. Success return

Extraction plan for preCliTestReworkSetup (pure planners, side effects stay in order):

- `buildReworkStartedComment(prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure: builds the Jira comment string (with conflicts panel). This has the conflicts loop.
- `decideNoPrOutcome(...)` — hmm, the no-PR flow has: ls-remote probe (side effect), tracker calls (side effect), checkout (side effect), createPr (side effect). 

Better approach following "Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor":
- `buildReworkStartedComment(ticketKey, prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure, testable.
- `buildBranchMissingError(testBranchName)` — trivial.
- The no-PR flow can be extracted into `ensureTestBranchAndPr(...)` — a helper function with its own CC, but then the helper needs to be covered by tests (which my characterization tests do — the auto-create paths are covered now).

CRAP = CC² + CC (at 0% coverage) — actually CRAP = CC² * (1 - cov)³ + CC - 1... the standard formula: CRAP = comp² * (1 - coverage)³ + comp. At 100% coverage CRAP = comp - 1. Hmm, for crap4js let me check the formula. Actually standard crap4j: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. At 0% coverage: CRAP = comp² + comp. At 100%: CRAP = comp − 1... 

For action with CC 51 at 17.5% coverage: 51² × (1-0.175)³ + 51 = 2601 × 0.5615 + 51 ≈ 1460 + 51 = 1511. ✓ matches 1512.8 (coverage slightly different).

To get action < 100:
- Option A: CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 8. Or CC 11 at ~90% coverage: 121 × 0.001 + 11 ≈ 11. 
- So I need to cut action's CC from 51 to ~≤10 AND have it well covered.

My characterization tests cover most paths of action. After extraction, the remaining action body will be: resolve params, load config/scm/tracker, clear stale outputs, repoInfo check, ensurePr (call helper), PR details check, checkout, conflicts, diff, discussions, context write, questions, bugs, comment, return. If I extract the no-PR flow into `ensureTestPullRequest(scm, tracker, config, ticketKey, inputFolder, cli)` and the comment building into a pure function, action's CC should drop to ~12-15. With coverage ~90%+, CRAP ≈ 15² × (0.1)³ + 14 = 0.15 + 14 ≈ 14. 

New functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP if untested → CC ≤ 2, or cover them. My tests will cover the extracted helpers well (through action and directly for pure ones). A helper with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP 11 — that's > 8, which FAILS the ratchet for NEW functions ("new functions must be <= 8")! 

Wait — re-read: "new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it)". So a new function with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 12 - 1 = 11 > 8 → blocked as newOverThreshold! Hmm, but that would mean EVERY extracted helper must have CRAP ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage. At 100% coverage, CRAP = CC - 1 ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9. OK so extracted helpers can have up to CC 9 if fully covered. That's fine.

But wait — is coverage in the node harness (with ~108 known mock-gap failures) going to give the helpers 100% coverage? Coverage of partially-covered helpers: a helper with CC 12 at 85% coverage → 144 × (0.15)³ + 11 = 0.486 + 11 = 11.5 → still > 8 → FAIL. So helpers need CC ≤ 8ish or very high coverage.

Rule of thumb for me: keep extracted helpers CC ≤ 9 and make sure tests cover all branches. For bigger extracted pieces (like the no-PR flow, CC ~20), split into multiple smaller helpers, OR ensure coverage is ~95%+: CC 20 at 95% → 400 × (0.05)³ + 19 = 0.05 + 19 ≈ 19 → still > 8. blocks.text:
While instrumentation runs, let me plan the refactoring. Let me analyze the complexity hotspots.

### `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` (CC 51, CRAP 1512.8)

The action has these phases:
1. Param/inputFolder/ticketKey resolution
2. Config/SCM/tracker creation
3. Stale output clearing (cli call)
4. repoInfo check
5. PR resolution: findTestPRForTicket or (no PR): branch-exists check → back-out to Backlog OR checkout (with fetch fallback) + auto-create PR (success → continue; fail → noPR return)
6. PR details fetch
7. Branch determination + checkout
8. Merge conflict detection + diff + discussions
9. Context write
10. Questions/bugs fetch
11. Jira comment build (with conflicts panel)
12. Success return

Extraction plan for preCliTestReworkSetup (pure planners, side effects stay in order):
- `resolveTicketContext(params)` — pure: resolves inputFolder/ticketKey. Small CC.
- `buildReworkStartedComment(prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure: builds the Jira comment string (with conflicts panel). This has the conflicts loop.
- `decideNoPrOutcome(...)` — hmm, the no-PR flow has: ls-remote probe (side effect), tracker calls (side effect), checkout (side effect), createPr (side effect). 

Better approach following "Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor":
- `buildReworkStartedComment(ticketKey, prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure, testable.
- `buildBranchMissingError(testBranchName)` — trivial.
- The no-PR flow can be extracted into `ensureTestBranchAndPr(...)` — a helper function with its own CC, but then the helper needs to be covered by tests (which my characterization tests do — the auto-create paths are covered now).

CRAP = CC² + CC (at 0% coverage) — actually CRAP = CC² * (1 - cov)³ + CC - 1... the standard formula: CRAP = comp² * (1 - coverage)³ + comp. At 100% coverage CRAP = comp - 1. Hmm, for crap4js let me check the formula. Actually standard crap4j: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. At 0% coverage: CRAP = comp² + comp. At 100%: CRAP = comp − 1... 

For action with CC 51 at 17.5% coverage: 51² × (1-0.175)³ + 51 = 2601 × 0.5615 + 51 ≈ 1460 + 51 = 1511. ✓ matches 1512.8 (coverage slightly different).

To get action < 100:
- Option A: CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 8. Or CC 11 at ~90% coverage: 121 × 0.001 + 11 ≈ 11. 
- So I need to cut action's CC from 51 to ~≤10 AND have it well covered.

My characterization tests cover most paths of action. After extraction, the remaining action body will be: resolve params, load config/scm/tracker, clear stale outputs, repoInfo check, ensurePr (call helper), PR details check, checkout, conflicts, diff, discussions, context write, questions, bugs, comment, return. If I extract the no-PR flow into `ensureTestPullRequest(scm, tracker, config, ticketKey, inputFolder, cli)` and the comment building into a pure function, action's CC should drop to ~12-15. With coverage ~90%+, CRAP ≈ 15² × (0.1)³ + 14 = 0.15 + 14 ≈ 14. 

New functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP if untested → CC ≤ 2, or cover them. My tests will cover the extracted helpers well (through action and directly for pure ones). A helper with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP 11 — that's > 8, which FAILS the ratchet for NEW functions ("new functions must be <= 8")! 

Wait — re-read: "new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it)". So a new function with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 12 - 1 = 11 > 8 → blocked as newOverThreshold! Hmm, but that would mean EVERY extracted helper must have CRAP ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage. At 100% coverage, CRAP = CC - 1 ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9. OK so extracted helpers can have up to CC 9 if fully covered. That's fine.

But wait — is coverage in the node harness (with ~108 known mock-gap failures) going to give the helpers 100% coverage? The coverage comes from the node harness run over ALL test files in run_all.json. My new tests will run there. Coverage of partially-covered helpers: a helper with CC 12 at 85% coverage → 144 × (0.15)³ + 11 = 0.486 + 11 = 11.5 → still > 8 → FAIL. So helpers need CC ≤ 8ish or very high coverage.

Rule of thumb for me: keep extracted helpers CC ≤ 9 and make sure tests cover all branches. For bigger extracted pieces (like the no-PR flow, CC ~20), split into multiple smaller helpers, OR ensure coverage is ~95%+: CC 20 at 95% → 400 × (0.05)³ + 19 = 0.05 + 19 ≈ 19 → still > 8. CRAP at high coverage ≈ CC - 1. So EVERY new function must have CC ≤ 9 regardless (given near-100% coverage). OK: max CC 9 per new function, fully covered.

Hmm wait, but also existing over-threshold functions I extract FROM: the ratchet only compares functions that exist in BOTH baseline and metrics. If I delete `action` (rename), the baseline key `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` would be "removed" — and `removed` doesn't fail. But the ticket wants `action` to remain (same exports/signatures). `action` will remain in the baseline with its key. Its score must go DOWN from 1512.8. If I re-extract so its CC drops to ~10 with ~95% coverage → CRAP ≈ 10 → improved. 

Also "no function may go up": `findTestPRForTicket` (30 in preCli file, 42 in post file) must not go up. I won't touch them, or may even improve them.

Extraction: `findOpenPRForBranch(openPrs, branchName)` (pure), `buildAutoPRTitle(ticket, ticketKey)` (pure), `buildFallbackPRShape(prResult, branchName)` (pure), `parsePrNumberFromUrl(url)` (pure). Let me now count action's branches and see what remains after extraction. I'll aim to bring action CC to ≤ 9ish, with all-branch characterization coverage.

Also there might be complexity sources I can restructure: `wipLabel` ternary, `releaseLock` closure (nested function adds CC to action? nested functions' CC might be counted separately... in crap4js, functions are counted per function declaration; nested function expressions might be attributed to the parent or separate — let me check how the analyzer handles nested functions).

While instrumentation runs, let me plan the refactoring. Let me analyze the complexity hotspots.

### `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` (CC 51, CRAP 1512.8)

The action has these phases:
1. Param/inputFolder/ticketKey resolution
2. Config/SCM/tracker creation
3. Stale output clearing (cli call)
4. repoInfo check
5. PR resolution: findTestPRForTicket or (no PR): branch-exists check → back-out to Backlog OR checkout (with fetch fallback) + auto-create PR (success → continue; fail → noPR return)
6. PR details fetch
7. Branch determination + checkout
8. Merge conflict detection + diff + discussions
9. Context write
10. Questions/bugs fetch
11. Jira comment build (with conflicts panel)
12. Success return

Extraction plan for preCliTestReworkSetup (pure planners, side effects stay in order):

blocks.text:
While instrumentation runs, let me plan the refactoring. Let me analyze the complexity hotspots.

### `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` (CC 51, CRAP 1512.8)

The action has these phases:
1. Param/inputFolder/ticketKey resolution
2. Config/SCM/tracker creation
3. Stale output clearing (cli call)
4. repoInfo check
5. PR resolution: findTestPRForTicket or (no PR): branch-exists check → back-out to Backlog OR checkout (with fetch fallback) + auto-create PR (success → continue; fail → noPR return)
6. PR details fetch
7. Branch determination + checkout
8. Merge conflict detection + diff + discussions
9. Context write
10. Questions/bugs fetch
11. Jira comment build (with conflicts panel)
12. Success return

Extraction plan for preCliTestReworkSetup (pure planners, side effects stay in order):
- `resolveTicketContext(params)` — pure: resolves inputFolder/ticketKey. Small CC.
- `buildReworkStartedComment(prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure: builds the Jira comment string (with conflicts panel). This has the conflicts loop.
- `decideNoPrOutcome(...)` — hmm, the no-PR flow has: ls-remote probe (side effect), tracker calls (side effect), checkout (side effect), createPr (side effect). 

Better approach following "Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor":
- `buildReworkStartedComment(ticketKey, prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure, testable.
- `buildBranchMissingError(testBranchName)` — trivial.
- The no-PR flow can be extracted into `ensureTestBranchAndPr(...)` — a helper function with its own CC, but then the helper needs to be covered by tests (which my characterization tests do — the auto-create paths are covered now).

CRAP = CC² + CC (at 0% coverage) — actually CRAP = CC² * (1 - cov)³ + CC - 1... the standard formula: CRAP = comp² * (1 - coverage)³ + comp. At 100% coverage CRAP = comp - 1. Hmm, for crap4js let me check the formula. Actually standard crap4j: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. At 0% coverage: CRAP = comp² + comp. At 100%: CRAP = comp − 1...

While instrumentation runs, let me plan the refactoring. Let me analyze the complexity hotspots.

### `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` (CC 51, CRAP 1512.8)

The action has these phases:
1. Param/inputFolder/ticketKey resolution
2. Config/SCM/tracker creation
3. Stale output clearing (cli call)
4. repoInfo check
5. PR resolution: findTestPRForTicket or (no PR): branch-exists check → back-out to Backlog OR checkout (with fetch fallback) + auto-create PR (success → continue; fail → noPR return)
6. PR details fetch
7. Branch determination + checkout
8. Merge conflict detection + diff + discussions
9. Context write
10. Questions/bugs fetch
11. Jira comment build (with conflicts panel)
12. Success return

Extraction plan for preCliTestReworkSetup (pure planners, side effects stay in order):
- `resolveTicketContext(params)` — pure: resolves inputFolder/ticketKey. Small CC.
- `buildReworkStartedComment(prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure: builds the Jira comment string (with conflicts panel). This has the conflicts loop.
- `decideNoPrOutcome(...)` — hmm, the no-PR flow has: ls-remote probe (side effect), tracker calls (side effect), checkout (side effect), createPr (side effect). 

Better approach following "Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor":
- `buildReworkStartedComment(ticketKey, prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure, testable.
- `buildBranchMissingError(testBranchName)` — trivial.
- The no-PR flow can be extracted into `ensureTestBranchAndPr(...)` — a helper function with its own CC, but then the helper needs to be covered by tests (which my characterization tests do — the auto-create paths are covered now).

CRAP = CC² + CC (at 0% coverage) — actually CRAP = CC² * (1 - cov)³ + CC - 1... the standard formula: CRAP = comp² * (1 - coverage)³ + comp. At 100% coverage CRAP = comp - 1. Hmm, for crap4js let me check the formula. Actually standard crap4j: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. At 0% coverage: CRAP = comp² + comp. At 100%: CRAP = comp − 1... 

For action with CC 51 at 17.5% coverage: 51² × (1-0.175)³ + 51 = 2601 × 0.5615 + 51 ≈ 1460 + 51 = 1511. ✓ matches 1512.8 (coverage slightly different).

To get action < 100:
- Option A: CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 8. Or CC 11 at ~90% coverage: 121 × 0.001 + 11 ≈ 11. 
- So I need to cut action's CC from 51 to ~≤10 AND have it well covered.

My characterization tests cover most paths of action. After extraction, the remaining action body will be: resolve params, load config/scm/tracker, clear stale outputs, repoInfo check, ensurePr (call helper), PR details check, checkout, conflicts, diff, discussions, context write, questions, bugs, comment, return. If I extract the no-PR flow into `ensureTestPullRequest(scm, tracker, config, ticketKey, inputFolder, cli)` and the comment building into a pure function, action's CC should drop to ~12-15. With coverage ~90%+, CRAP ≈ 15² × (0.1)³ + 14 = 0.15 + 14 ≈ 14. 

New functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP if untested → CC ≤ 2, or cover them. My tests will cover the extracted helpers well (through action and directly for pure ones). A helper with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP 11 — that's > 8, which FAILS the ratchet for NEW functions ("new functions must be <= 8")! 

Wait — re-read: "new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it)". So a new function with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 12 - 1 = 11 > 8 → blocked as newOverThreshold! Hmm, but that would mean EVERY extracted helper must have CRAP ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage. At 100% coverage, CRAP = CC - 1 ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9. OK so extracted helpers can have up to CC 9 if fully covered. That's fine.

But wait — is coverage in the node harness (with ~108 known mock-gap failures) going to give the helpers 100% coverage? The coverage comes from the node harness run over ALL test files in run_all.json. My new tests will run there. Coverage of partially-covered helpers: a helper with CC 12 at 85% coverage → 144 × (0.15)³ + 11 = 0.486 + 11 = 11.5 → still > 8 → FAIL. So helpers need CC ≤ 8ish or very high coverage.

Rule of thumb for me: keep extracted helpers CC ≤ 9 and make sure tests cover all branches. For bigger extracted pieces (like the no-PR flow, CC ~20), split into multiple smaller helpers, OR ensure coverage is ~95%+: CC 20 at 95% → 400 × (0.05)³ + 19 = 0.05 + 19 ≈ 19 → still > 8. CRAP at high coverage ≈ CC - 1. So EVERY new function must have CC ≤ 9 regardless (given near-100% coverage). OK: max CC 9 per new function, fully covered.

Hmm wait, but also existing over-threshold functions I extract FROM: the ratchet only compares functions that exist in BOTH baseline and metrics. If I delete `action` (rename), the baseline key `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` would be "removed" — and `removed` doesn't fail. But the ticket wants `action` to remain (same exports/signatures). `action` will remain in the baseline with its key. Its score must go DOWN from 1512.8. If I re-extract so its CC drops to ~10 with ~95% coverage → CRAP ≈ 10 → improved. 

Also "no function may go up": `findTestPRForTicket` (30 in preCli file, 42 in post file) must not go up. I won't touch them, or may even improve them.

blocks.text:
While instrumentation runs, let me plan the refactoring. Let me analyze the complexity hotspots.

### `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` (CC 51, CRAP 1512.8)

The action has these phases:
1. Param/inputFolder/ticketKey resolution
2. Config/SCM/tracker creation
3. Stale output clearing (cli call)
4. repoInfo check
5. PR resolution: findTestPRForTicket or (no PR): branch-exists check → back-out to Backlog OR checkout (with fetch fallback) + auto-create PR (success → continue; fail → noPR return)
6. PR details fetch
7. Branch determination + checkout
8. Merge conflict detection + diff + discussions
9. Context write
10. Questions/bugs fetch
11. Jira comment build (with conflicts panel)
12. Success return

Extraction plan for preCliTestReworkSetup (pure planners, side effects stay in order):
- `resolveTicketContext(params)` — pure: resolves inputFolder/ticketKey. Small CC.
- `buildReworkStartedComment(prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure: builds the Jira comment string (with conflicts panel). This has the conflicts loop.
- `decideNoPrOutcome(...)` — hmm, the no-PR flow has: ls-remote probe (side effect), tracker calls (side effect), checkout (side effect), createPr (side effect). 

Better approach following "Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor":
- `buildReworkStartedComment(ticketKey, prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure, testable.
- `buildBranchMissingError(testBranchName)` — trivial.
- The no-PR flow can be extracted into `ensureTestBranchAndPr(...)` — a helper function with its own CC, but then the helper needs to be covered by tests (which my characterization tests do — the auto-create paths are covered now).

CRAP = CC² + CC (at 0% coverage) — actually CRAP = CC² * (1 - cov)³ + CC - 1... the standard formula: CRAP = comp² * (1 - coverage)³ + comp. At 100% coverage CRAP = comp - 1. Hmm, for crap4js let me check the formula. Actually standard crap4j: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. At 0% coverage: CRAP = comp² + comp. At 100%: CRAP = comp − 1... 

For action with CC 51 at 17.5% coverage: 51² × (1-0.175)³ + 51 = 2601 × 0.5615 + 51 ≈ 1460 + 51 = 1511. ✓ matches 1512.8 (coverage slightly different).

To get action < 100:
- Option A: CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 8. Or CC 11 at ~90% coverage: 121 × 0.001 + 11 ≈ 11. 
- So I need to cut action's CC from 51 to ~≤10 AND have it well covered.

My characterization tests cover most paths of action. After extraction, the remaining action body will be: resolve params, load config/scm/tracker, clear stale outputs, repoInfo check, ensurePr (call helper), PR details check, checkout, conflicts, diff, discussions, context write, questions, bugs, comment, return. If I extract the no-PR flow into `ensureTestPullRequest(scm, tracker, config, ticketKey, inputFolder, cli)` and the comment building into a pure function, action's CC should drop to ~12-15. With coverage ~90%+, CRAP ≈ 15² × (0.1)³ + 14 = 0.15 + 14 ≈ 14. 

New functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP if untested → CC ≤ 2, or cover them. My tests will cover the extracted helpers well (through action and directly for pure ones). A helper with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP 11 — that's > 8, which FAILS the ratchet for NEW functions ("new functions must be <= 8")! 

Wait — re-read: "new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it)". So a new function with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 12 - 1 = 11 > 8 → blocked as newOverThreshold! Hmm, but that would mean EVERY extracted helper must have CRAP ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage. At 100% coverage, CRAP = CC - 1 ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9. OK so extracted helpers can have up to CC 9 if fully covered. That's fine.

But wait — is coverage in the node harness (with ~108 known mock-gap failures) going to give the helpers 100% coverage? The coverage comes from the node harness run over ALL test files in run_all.json. My new tests will run there. Coverage of partially-covered helpers: a helper with CC 12 at 85% coverage → 144 × (0.15)³ + 11 = 0.486 + 11 = 11.5 → still > 8 → FAIL. So helpers need CC ≤ 8ish or very high coverage.

Rule of thumb for me: keep extracted helpers CC ≤ 9 and make sure tests cover all branches. For bigger extracted pieces (like the no-PR flow, CC ~20), split into multiple smaller helpers, OR ensure coverage is ~95%+: CC 20 at 95% → 400 × (0.05)³ + 19 = 0.05 + 19 ≈ 19 → still > 8. CRAP at high coverage ≈ CC - 1. So EVERY new function must have CC ≤ 9 regardless (given near-100% coverage). OK: max CC 9 per new function, fully covered.

Hmm wait, but also existing over-threshold functions I extract FROM: the ratchet only compares functions that exist in BOTH baseline and metrics. If I delete `action` (rename), the baseline key `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` would be "removed" — and `removed` doesn't fail. But the ticket wants `action` to remain (same exports/signatures). `action` will remain in the baseline with its key. Its score must go DOWN from 1512.8. If I re-extract so its CC drops to ~10 with ~95% coverage → CRAP ≈ 10 → improved. 

Also "no function may go up": `findTestPRForTicket` (30 in preCli file, 42 in post file) must not go up. I won't touch them, or may even improve them.

blocks.text:
While instrumentation runs, let me plan the refactoring. Let me analyze the complexity hotspots.

### `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` (CC 51, CRAP 1512.8)

The action has these phases:
1. Param/inputFolder/ticketKey resolution
2. Config/SCM/tracker creation
3. Stale output clearing (cli call)
4. repoInfo check
5. PR resolution: findTestPRForTicket or (no PR): branch-exists check → back-out to Backlog OR checkout (with fetch fallback) + auto-create PR (success → continue; fail → noPR return)
6. PR details fetch
7. Branch determination + checkout
8. Merge conflict detection + diff + discussions
9. Context write
10. Questions/bugs fetch
11. Jira comment build (with conflicts panel)
12. Success return

Extraction plan for preCliTestReworkSetup (pure planners, side effects stay in order):
- `resolveTicketContext(params)` — pure: resolves inputFolder/ticketKey. Small CC.
- `buildReworkStartedComment(prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure: builds the Jira comment string (with conflicts panel). This has the conflicts loop.
- `decideNoPrOutcome(...)` — hmm, the no-PR flow has: ls-remote probe (side effect), tracker calls (side effect), checkout (side effect), createPr (side effect). 

Better approach following "Extract pure planners/parsers; keep side effects in a thin executor":
- `buildReworkStartedComment(ticketKey, prDetails, branchName, conflictFiles)` — pure, testable.
- `buildBranchMissingError(testBranchName)` — trivial.
- The no-PR flow can be extracted into `ensureTestBranchAndPr(...)` — a helper function with its own CC, but then the helper needs to be covered by tests (which my characterization tests do — the auto-create paths are covered now).

CRAP = CC² + CC (at 0% coverage) — actually CRAP = CC² * (1 - cov)³ + CC - 1... the standard formula: CRAP = comp² * (1 - coverage)³ + comp. At 100% coverage CRAP = comp - 1. Hmm, for crap4js let me check the formula. Actually standard crap4j: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. At 0% coverage: CRAP = comp² + comp. At 100%: CRAP = comp − 1... 

For action with CC 51 at 17.5% coverage: 51² × (1-0.175)³ + 51 = 2601 × 0.5615 + 51 ≈ 1460 + 51 = 1511. ✓ matches 1512.8 (coverage slightly different).

To get action < 100:
- Option A: CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 8. Or CC 11 at ~90% coverage: 121 × 0.001 + 11 ≈ 11. 
- So I need to cut action's CC from 51 to ~≤10 AND have it well covered.

My characterization tests cover most paths of action. After extraction, the remaining action body will be: resolve params, load config/scm/tracker, clear stale outputs, repoInfo check, ensurePr (call helper), PR details check, checkout, conflicts, diff, discussions, context write, questions, bugs, comment, return. If I extract the no-PR flow into `ensureTestPullRequest(scm, tracker, config, ticketKey, inputFolder, cli)` and the comment building into a pure function, action's CC should drop to ~12-15. With coverage ~90%+, CRAP ≈ 15² × (0.1)³ + 14 = 0.15 + 14 ≈ 14. 

New functions must be ≤ 8 CRAP if untested → CC ≤ 2, or cover them. My tests will cover the extracted helpers well (through action and directly for pure ones). A helper with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP 11 — that's > 8, which FAILS the ratchet for NEW functions ("new functions must be <= 8")! 

Wait — re-read: "new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it)". So a new function with CC 12 at 100% coverage → CRAP = 12 - 1 = 11 > 8 → blocked as newOverThreshold! Hmm, but that would mean EVERY extracted helper must have CRAP ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9 at 100% coverage. At 100% coverage, CRAP = CC - 1 ≤ 8 → CC ≤ 9. OK so extracted helpers can have up to CC 9 if fully covered. That's fine.

But wait — is coverage in the node harness (with ~108 known mock-gap failures) going to give the helpers 100% coverage? The coverage comes from the node harness run over ALL test files in run_all.json. My new tests will run there. Coverage of partially-covered helpers: a helper with CC 12 at 85% coverage → 144 × (0.15)³ + 11 = 0.486 + 11 = 11.5 → still > 8 → FAIL. So helpers need CC ≤ 8ish or very high coverage.

Rule of thumb for me: keep extracted helpers CC ≤ 9 and make sure tests cover all branches. For bigger extracted pieces (like the no-PR flow, CC ~20), split into multiple smaller helpers, OR ensure coverage is ~95%+: CC 20 at 95% → 400 × (0.05)³ + 19 = 0.05 + 19 ≈ 19 → still > 8. CRAP at high coverage ≈ CC - 1. So EVERY new function must have CC ≤ 9 regardless (given near-100% coverage). OK: max CC 9 per new function, fully covered.

Hmm wait, but also existing over-threshold functions I extract FROM: the ratchet only compares functions that exist in BOTH baseline and metrics. If I delete `action` (rename), the baseline key `js/preCliTestReworkSetup.js::action` would be "removed" — and `removed` doesn't fail. But the ticket wants `action` to remain (same exports/signatures). `action` will remain in the baseline with its key. Its score must go DOWN from 1512.8. If I re-extract so its CC drops to ~10 with ~95% coverage → CRAP ≈ 10 → improved. 

Also "no function may go up": `findTestPRForTicket` (30 in preCli file, 42 in post file) must not go up. I won't touch them, or may even improve them.
